note: How a story moves from a search result to a published page, and who owns each move. Every state names the one role that can advance it and the door it has to get through — the condition that must be true before the next role will take it. A story can only be in one state; the desk records which.

states.label: Spotted
states.means: A candidate exists. Somebody searched and something came back.
states.door: A specific artefact can be named — not a topic, an artefact.

states.label: Registered
states.means: The source is in the register with a state and a checked date, and the URL resolved.
states.door: The fetch returned 200. A blocked or dead URL cannot pass — that is gate check 7.

states.label: Frozen
states.means: A byte copy is held and hashed, with the retrieval time recorded.
states.door: The hash exists and the bytes are stored.
states.blocked_why: The fetch-freeze-hash path is not built. Every story is stuck at this door, which is why nothing in the graph is anchored and every fact reads secondary.

states.label: Extracted
states.means: Typed nodes and edges exist, conforming to the ontology, anchored where a frozen copy allows it.
states.door: Every verb is in the vocabulary and every node names its source. Gate checks 1 and 2.

states.label: Drafted
states.means: Prose exists in markdown, and names the node ids it stands on.
states.door: Every sentence traces to a node. Gate check 3.

states.label: Cleared
states.means: The refusal list has been applied and nothing on it was triggered.
states.door: No named organisation is assessed; no severity language that the graph does not compute; no implication of human review.

states.label: Gated
states.means: Both gates pass — the section's own checks and the whole-site gate.
states.door: Exit zero. A failing gate is answered, never silenced.

states.label: Published
states.means: Live, versioned, and carrying the beta and no-human-review notices.
states.door: The version was bumped and the release note says what is still missing.

states.label: Superseded
states.means: A later fact replaced one this story rests on. The story stays up; the superseding edge is added.
states.door: Never delete. The original remains readable and the edge points forward.

states.label: Parked
states.means: Not dead, not moving. Waiting on something outside this newsroom.
states.door: The blocker is named, so a reader can see what would unblock it.

states.label: Refused
states.means: Killed on the refusal list. Recorded rather than quietly dropped.
states.door: The refusal that bit is named. Cut, never softened.
